title: Plan the rows before you dig

unit.title: Plan the rows before you dig
unit.needIt: Ten minutes with a pencil decides how much food a small plot gives you, and how hard it is to work in all summer.
unit.why: A gardener wants to grow a lot of food but has a small space. They learn that placing plants in rows helps them use tools to clear weeds quickly. By planning the direction of the rows, they make sure every plant gets enough sunlight to grow big.
unit.outcome: Design a garden layout that maximizes space and sunlight.
unit.reachesYou: You see this when you organize your kitchen shelves to reach your favorite snacks. You also see it when you plan a path through a crowded store.
unit.do: Draw a simple map of a small space you want to use. Mark out narrow paths and rows to see how much room is left for plants.

quiz.q: What is the chief aim when laying out a small garden?
choices: To use every bit of soil
To grow only one type of plant
quiz.why: The text says the goal is to use all available soil by making paths just wide enough to walk in.
quiz.quote: Here the chief aim will be to make use of every available bit of soil

quiz.q: Why is it better to run rows from north to south?
choices: It lets sun reach the ground
quiz.why: North to south rows allow the sun to reach the ground lengthwise between the rows.
quiz.quote: This enables the sun to get at the eround lengthwise of the rows, and between them

quiz.q: How should you arrange plants based on their height?
choices: Put tall plants at the back
Put tall plants in the middle
Put tall plants at the front
Put tall plants at the side
quiz.why: The text suggests putting corn at the side and then working down to lower plants.
quiz.quote: Give corn a place at the side of the garden.

quiz.q: How much space should be left between rows for a cultivator?
quiz.why: The text specifies eighteen inches to allow the tool to work properly.
quiz.quote: If the garden-cultivator is to be used, leave a space about eighteen inches wide between the rows to work in.

quiz.q: What does the garden-cultivator do to the soil?
choices: It cuts the weeds in half
It stirs the soil and uproots weeds
quiz.why: The cultivator is a labor-saving tool that stirs soil and removes weeds at once.
quiz.quote: this implement stirs the soil and uproots weeds at the same time.

quiz.q: What is a weeding-hook used for?
choices: To do weeding in a short time
quiz.why: The weeding-hook is a cheap tool that allows for fast weeding without hand-pulling.
quiz.quote: It enables one to do a good deal of weeding in a short time

partials: Make paths just wide enough to walk.
Run rows north and south for sun.
crystal.key: Plan the layout to maximize space, sunlight, and ease of work.

decoys.text: Make paths as wide as possible.
decoys.why: The text says paths should be just wide enough to walk in to save soil space.

decoys.text: Run rows east to west for better sun.
decoys.why: The text says east to west rows would shade the ground except for the first row.

crystal.aha: By planning the layout carefully, you ensure every plant gets sun and every task is easier to do.

scene.analogy: Packing a car trunk for a trip

actors.label: A minute of planning saves the space.

beats.say: An empty trunk and a pile of bags.
You look first, and decide what goes where.
Now it all fits, and you can still reach everything.

s2.sub: and you can reach it all

beats.say: Plan narrow paths and sunlit rows, and every bit of soil works.

line.label: Rows run north and south, for sun.
